title: Manager break corrections are wrongly refused when a session has more than one break.
scenario: Omar takes a tea break from 10:00 to 10:10 and a lunch break from 13:00 to 13:30. Tom tries to correct the lunch start to 13:05, but the system refuses because 13:05 is after the end of the tea break. Correcting the tea break's end to 10:12 is also refused because it is before the lunch start. Tom cannot fix break times, so Omar's paid minutes stay wrong.
test_needed: A session with two break pairs: correcting the second BREAK_START to a time inside the second break succeeds.

owner_question.question: Omar took a tea break and a lunch break. Tom needs to move the lunch start by five minutes. What should happen?
options: Allow it: only check against that break's own end and against clock in and clock out
Allow it, and also block any overlap between the two breaks
Keep today's behaviour: refuse the correction

title: Anyone at the counter kiosk can start or end a break for a locum or cross-site worker without any PIN.
scenario: Sara, a locum with a confirmed shift, clocks in by phone QR and has no membership PIN at Tom's pharmacy. The kiosk staff list shows her worker ID, and anyone at the counter (for example Mia) can tap break start for Sara with no PIN asked. Sara's unpaid break time begins without her knowing. Nadia, covering from Tom's other pharmacy, has the same problem because only a local membership PIN is checked.
test_needed: A break START from the kiosk for a clocked-in worker with no local membership PIN is refused unless that worker proves who they are.

owner_question.question: Sara is clocked in at Tom's pharmacy and has no kiosk PIN there. Mia taps 'start break' for Sara on the counter kiosk. What should happen?
options: Refuse: the worker must confirm with their own PIN or app
Allow it but tell Sara and flag it for Tom to review
Keep today's behaviour: allow it with no check

title: A repeated kiosk PIN submit flips the worker's clock state instead of being treated as a retry.
scenario: Omar types his PIN at Tom's kiosk and presses Clock, but the screen lags (or the kiosk resends after a slow network), so the same request arrives twice. The first request clocks him in. The second one sees an open session and clocks him straight back out, leaving a session of almost zero minutes while Omar thinks he is on the clock. The same thing happens at clock-out: a repeated request starts a new session that stays open overnight, so Tom's timesheet shows hours Omar never worked.
test_needed: Send POST kiosk/pin-clock/ twice within 5 seconds with the same PIN and check that exactly one CLOCK_IN exists and the session is still open.

owner_question.question: Omar presses Clock twice within a few seconds at Tom's kiosk. What should happen?
options: The second press within 30 seconds counts as the same action; Omar stays clocked in
The kiosk asks Omar to confirm before clocking out someone who clocked in under a minute ago
Keep today's behaviour: each press flips Omar between clocked in and clocked out

title: The kiosk staff lookup reveals staff names and masked emails by guessable number, and sends setup emails without a dedicated rate limit.
scenario: Anyone standing at the paired counter tablet in Tom's pharmacy can type 1, 2, 3 and so on into the Staff ID box. For Omar, Ali, Mia, and also Nadia at Tom's other pharmacy, the kiosk shows the full name, account number and a partly hidden email. Unknown numbers get a different 'not found' answer, so every staff member in the group can be listed. Anyone who has no PIN yet (for example a new starter like Jack) gets a setup-code email on every probe. The PIN clock screen deliberately gives one generic error so this cannot happen, but the lookup screen undoes that.
test_needed: Using one device token, look up a known staff ID and an unknown one and assert both answers look the same with no name or email; then assert repeated lookups are rate-limited like the PIN screen.

owner_question.question: Someone at Tom's counter tablet types Staff ID numbers one after another. What should the kiosk show them?
options: Nothing that names anyone: the same neutral 'enter your PIN or check your email' answer for every number, rate-limited
Show names only for staff of this pharmacy, never staff from Tom's other pharmacies, and rate-limit lookups
Keep today's behaviour: show the name and partly hidden email so staff can confirm it is them

title: The kiosk login check also accepts the stored token text as-is, so the scrambled copy saved in the database works as a kiosk token.
scenario: Kiosk tokens are saved only in scrambled (hashed) form so that a leaked database or backup can't be used to sign in a kiosk. But the login check also accepts a token that matches the saved text exactly. So anyone who sees the saved value for Tom's front-counter kiosk (in a backup, an admin screen or a support export) can send it as the token and act as that kiosk: show sign-in QR codes, look up staff and clock people in. Nothing hashes old plain-text tokens, so this extra check is permanent.
test_needed: Activate a kiosk, read its saved hash from the database, call authenticate_kiosk_device with that hash and assert it returns None.

owner_question.question: If someone gets a copy of Tom's database backup, should the kiosk token values in it be enough to run Tom's counter kiosk?
options: No: hash the old plain-text tokens once and accept only real tokens from then on
No: make old unhashed kiosks pair again, then drop the extra check
Keep today's behaviour so very old kiosks keep working

title: Anyone with one active membership can pull any pharmacy's staff into a custom group and harvest their names and emails.
scenario: Sara has one active membership somewhere. She creates a custom group chat and lists membership numbers from many pharmacies, including Nadia at Tom's other pharmacy. Each person is added with no check that Sara shares a pharmacy with them. Sara then opens her chat participants list and sees each person's name, email, photo and job type, and can message all of them.
test_needed: Sara creates a group with Nadia's membership id from an unrelated pharmacy; expect 400/403 and no Participant row for Nadia.

owner_question.question: When Sara builds a custom group chat, whom should she be allowed to add?
options: Only people she shares an accepted pharmacy membership with
Only people she already has a DM or shift with
Anyone on the platform (keep today's behaviour)

title: A shift checkout without selected offers charges one fee but confirms every worker waiting for payment.
scenario: Tom's shift has three slots, each with a worker waiting on payment. If checkout is started without naming offers or slots, Stripe charges a single fee. When it is paid, all three workers are confirmed. With slots named, two workers waiting on the same slot are also both confirmed for one fee. ChemistTasker is underpaid for each extra worker.
test_needed: Shift with 3 awaiting offers on 3 slots: POST charge-fulfillment with {} and expect a 400 or quantity 3, not quantity 1 that finalizes 3.

owner_question.question: Tom pays the fee once while three workers are waiting on his shift. What should happen?
options: Require Tom to pick the workers, and charge one fee per worker
Charge for all waiting workers automatically
One fee confirms everyone (keep today's behaviour)

title: An organisation's free trial depends on which org admin clicks pay, so a newly joined admin makes every shift free.
scenario: Lina's organisation has been on ChemistTasker for a year. A newly created org admin account, under 30 days old, pays a shift fee for Tom's pharmacy, and the shift is confirmed free as a 'free trial'. This can be repeated with each new admin account. The same shift costs money if a chief admin or Lina pays instead.
test_needed: Org created long ago, new ORG_ADMIN joined today pays fulfilment; expect PAYMENT_REQUIRED, not FREE_TRIAL.

owner_question.question: Lina's year-old organisation adds a new admin, who pays a shift fee. Should it be free?
options: No: the trial follows the organisation's start date
Trial follows the first org admin only
Yes: it follows whoever pays (keep today's behaviour)

title: Organisation billing falls back to the pharmacy owner's personal subscription for viewing, seat purchases and subscriber status.
scenario: Tom has his own active subscription, and his pharmacy belongs to Lina's organisation, which has none. Lina's org billing page shows Tom's subscription and its payment-provider ids as the organisation's. When Lina buys extra seats, the checkout runs on Tom's payment customer, and the seats may land on the organisation's record without any base plan.
test_needed: Org without subscription, owner with active one: ORG_ADMIN GET subscription returns inactive/none, and seat purchase is refused.

owner_question.question: Tom pays for his own plan and his pharmacy is in Lina's organisation. What should Lina's org billing show?
options: Only the organisation's own subscription (none)
Tom's plan, read-only, with no seat changes
Tom's plan, fully manageable (keep today's behaviour)

title: Deleting the owner's user account deletes all their shift payment records.
scenario: Tom paid fulfilment fees and penalties, including fees paid for organisation pharmacies, which are recorded under the pharmacy owner. If Tom's account is deleted, every payment record tied to him is deleted too. ChemistTasker loses the financial history it needs for refunds, disputes and tax records.
test_needed: Delete a user with ShiftPayment rows; expect the payments to remain (protected or owner set null).

owner_question.question: Tom deletes his account after paying shift fees. What should happen to those payment records?
options: Keep them, with Tom's identity anonymised
Block account deletion while payment records exist
Delete them with the account (keep today's behaviour)

title: Any chat member can rewrite who is in a room through the plain room update, skipping the creator/admin check and the community-chat block.
scenario: Mia, an ordinary assistant at Tom's pharmacy, edits the pharmacy's community chat through the standard room-edit call. She removes every member except the creator and adds Sara, an outside locum, by picking any active membership on the platform. Sara can now read the whole community chat history through the message list, even though she has no role at Tom's pharmacy. The same call also lets a non-admin member of a custom group rename it or remove the other members. The dedicated group-edit path would have refused both.
test_needed: As a non-admin, non-creator staff member, PATCH /rooms/<community_chat_id>/ with participants=[outsider_membership_id]. Expect 403, no new Participant row for the outsider, and no change to existing participants.

owner_question.question: Mia is a regular staff member, not a chat admin. She tries to change the members of Tom's pharmacy community chat, or of a custom group Omar created. What should happen?
options: Refuse: only the group creator or a group admin (or a pharmacy admin with comms rights, for community chats) can change members or the title
Let Mia add people from her own pharmacy only, and never remove anyone
Keep today's behaviour: any member can change the member list and title

title: Editing a poll, even just to fix a typo in the question, deletes every vote already cast.
scenario: Tom posts a poll in his pharmacy hub and Omar, Ali and Mia vote. Tom opens Edit to fix a spelling mistake in the question and saves. Web and mobile always resend the option list, so the server deletes all votes and rebuilds the options. The poll goes back to zero votes and nobody is warned.
test_needed: PATCH a poll that has votes, sending the same option labels and a new question; assert the votes and vote counts are kept.

owner_question.question: Tom edits a poll that Omar, Ali and Mia have already voted on. What should happen to their votes?
options: Votes are kept when the options are unchanged; only changed options lose their votes
Options are locked once anyone has voted; only the question can change
Keep today's behaviour: every edit clears all votes, but show Tom a warning first

title: Tagging teammates fails when editing a post, and when a new post has a file and exactly one tag.
scenario: Tom edits his pharmacy hub post on mobile to tag Omar and gets 'Unable to determine post scope for tagging', so the edit is refused. Separately, Tom writes a new post on web with a photo and tags only Omar. The upload turns the single tag into plain text instead of a list, so the post is rejected. It works only with no attachment or with two or more tags.
test_needed: PATCH an existing pharmacy post with tagged_member_ids=[staff id], and multipart-POST a post with one attachment and one tagged_member_ids value; both should return 200/201.

owner_question.question: Tom edits a post to tag Omar, or posts a photo tagging only Omar. What should happen?
options: Both work and Omar is notified
Tags can only be added when a post is first created; the edit screen hides tagging
Keep today's behaviour (both requests fail with an error)

title: Comment alerts with the comment text still go to a post's author after they lose access to that private hub.
scenario: Nadia wrote a post in her pharmacy's private hub and later left that pharmacy. Mia comments on the old post. Nadia's account is still active, so she gets an alert with the first 280 characters of Mia's internal comment and a link to a hub she can no longer open. The only check is whether the author's account is active, not whether they can still see the hub.
test_needed: Make the post author's membership inactive, comment as another member, and assert the former author gets no notification.

owner_question.question: Nadia left the pharmacy, but her old hub post gets a new comment from Mia. Should Nadia hear about it?
options: No alert once she can no longer see that hub
An alert with no comment text (just 'someone commented')
Keep today's behaviour (alert includes the comment text)

title: The editorial seed command has no production guard and changes admin access, live articles and comments under real users' names.
scenario: An operator runs the seed command on the live server, maybe after copying it from a setup note. If the hard-coded author emails do not exist, the very first account in the database (for example Tom) silently becomes a full content administrator, with publishing, invitation and moderation powers. Live launch guides are overwritten with localhost cover images, and made-up 'news' plus sample comments and reactions are posted under real members' accounts. Readers see fake regulatory news and comments that real pharmacists never wrote.
test_needed: Run seed_editorial_content with production settings (DEBUG off, not public_hub.test_settings) and assert that it raises CommandError and makes no ContentAdministrator, Article or Comment changes.

owner_question.question: If someone runs the editorial seed command on the live site, what should happen to Tom's account, the published guides and the comments shown to readers?
options: Refuse to run outside local/test settings, like the hub preview seed
Allow it on live only with an explicit --i-know flag, and never grant admin or post comments as real users
Keep today's behaviour (seed runs anywhere)

title: After a board report is resolved, the same user can never report that talent post or job shift again, yet is told the report was received.
scenario: Sara reports a job board shift Tom posted, and a moderator resolves it without hiding it. Tom later edits the shift description into something abusive. When Sara reports it again she sees 'Report received', but the system only finds her old resolved report, so nothing new reaches the moderators.
test_needed: Create a BoardReport by Sara, mark it resolved, have Sara POST the report again, and assert that an unresolved report now appears in the moderation queue.

owner_question.question: Sara's report on a job shift was dismissed, and the shift then changed. When she reports it again, what should happen?
options: A new open report reaches the moderators
Sara's old report reopens with her new reason
Keep today's behaviour (silently ignored, but she is told it was received)

title: Concurrent referral claims can award the same referral twice
scenario: Tom shares his friend referral with Sara. Sara has a verified account and submits the same claim twice at the same time. Both claims can succeed, giving Tom two 100-Pill rewards for referring Sara once; the extra credit can pay for shifts.
test_needed: Submit two concurrent first claims by verified Sara for Tom's same referral code, synchronizing their initial lookups; assert one claimed referral and one 100-Pill credit.

owner_question.question: When Sara submits Tom's same referral claim twice simultaneously, what should Tom receive?
options: One reward, with both submissions resolving to the same referral
One reward, with the duplicate submission rejected
Two rewards (keep today's behaviour)

title: Manual rostering allows staff to fill a pharmacist vacancy without pharmacist eligibility
scenario: Tom submits a manual roster assignment putting Ali into a pharmacist vacancy. Ali's accepted technician membership satisfies the checks, so the assignment succeeds without checking that Ali can perform pharmacist work.
test_needed: Manually assign accepted technician Ali to a pharmacist vacancy and assert rejection with no assignment created.

owner_question.question: When Tom manually puts Ali into a pharmacist vacancy, what should happen?
options: Reject because Ali is not a pharmacist
Require Tom to change the vacancy to technician work first
Allow Ali to fill the pharmacist vacancy (keep today's behaviour)

title: One claimed slot prevents claims on every remaining free slot
scenario: Tom posts two independently claimable pharmacist dates. Omar claims the first date, then tries to claim the second. The second claim is refused because the shift already has an assignment, although that date remains free.
test_needed: Claim one slot in a non-single-user shift, then claim another free slot and assert success.

owner_question.question: After Omar claims the first of Tom's independently claimable dates, what should happen to the second?
options: Keep the second date available for claims
Require Tom to offer the remaining date manually
Block all further claims on the shift (keep today's behaviour)

title: Recurring vacancies disappear from worker boards after their starting date
scenario: Tom posts an unfilled weekly pharmacist vacancy running for several weeks. Once its starting date passes, Sara cannot find the remaining dates on the public board. Omar likewise loses an equivalent recurring vacancy from the community board.
test_needed: Create an unassigned recurring slot starting yesterday with a future occurrence and assert it remains discoverable on worker boards.

owner_question.question: When Tom's recurring vacancy has future unfilled dates but its starting date has passed, what should Sara see?
options: The remaining future dates
A new advertisement Tom must publish for each date
No vacancy after the starting date passes (keep today's behaviour)

title: Public boards compare local shift times against the UTC clock
scenario: Tom posts a Sydney shift ending at 5 pm. At 6 pm Sydney time, Sara can still find and express interest in it because the board compares its ending time with the much earlier UTC clock.
test_needed: Freeze time at 6 pm Sydney time and assert a same-day shift ending at 5 pm is absent from both public lists.

owner_question.question: At 6 pm in Tom's pharmacy, should Sara still see a shift that ended there at 5 pm?
options: Hide it using the pharmacy's local time
Show it as closed and prevent applications
Keep it open until the UTC comparison expires (keep today's behaviour)

title: Accepting a valid counter offer for a vacancy without dated slots crashes
scenario: Tom posts a full-time vacancy without dated shifts. Sara submits a counter offer containing the requested working times but no date, which the app accepts. When Tom accepts it, the request fails instead of sending Sara an offer.
test_needed: Submit a valid slotless counter offer without slot_date, then accept it and assert a controlled successful response instead of an exception.

owner_question.question: When Sara counters Tom's full-time vacancy without dated shifts, what should accepting it do?
options: Send Sara an offer without requiring a shift date
Require a date before allowing the counter offer submission
Leave the submitted counter offer unacceptable (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirming one recurring date books dates outside the accepted terms
scenario: Sara counters for just one date in Tom's recurring vacancy, and Tom accepts that date. Sara reviews terms describing that date and confirms. When the booking is finalized, the app assigns Sara to every unfilled date in the recurring series, including dates she did not accept.
test_needed: Confirm an offer targeting one recurring occurrence and assert no assignments exist for any other occurrence.

owner_question.question: When Sara accepts terms for one date in Tom's recurring vacancy, which dates should she be booked for?
options: Only the date she accepted
The whole series after separately reviewing and accepting every date
Every unfilled recurring date immediately (keep today's behaviour)

title: Public shift responses expose other workers' names and email addresses.
scenario: Tom posts a public shift with several vacancies, and Ben confirms one while payment is pending. Sara browses that shift without joining Tom's pharmacy. The response reveals Ben's name and email; it also exposes contact details for workers already assigned.
test_needed: Retrieve a public shift as unrelated Sara and assert Ben's pending-payment and assignment contact details are absent.

owner_question.question: When Sara browses Tom's public vacancy, whose contact details should she see?
options: Only her own; Tom's managers can see other candidates
Confirmed coworkers' details after Sara is booked
Every candidate's details while browsing (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirmed counteroffers are invoiced using the original shift hours.
scenario: Tom advertises a flexible shift from 09:00 to 17:00. Sara proposes 10:00 to 14:00, Tom accepts, and Sara confirms. Her booking retains the original hours, and its invoice preview charges Tom for eight hours instead of the agreed four.
test_needed: Confirm a 10:00–14:00 counteroffer against a 09:00–17:00 slot and assert the booking and invoice use four hours.

owner_question.question: After Tom and Sara agree to shorten the shift, which hours should her booking and invoice use?
options: The agreed 10:00–14:00 hours
Require Tom to amend the vacancy before confirmation
The original 09:00–17:00 hours (keep today's behaviour)

title: Confirming one recurring occurrence books the worker for the entire series.
scenario: Tom posts a recurring Monday vacancy. Sara proposes working only the second Monday, and Tom accepts that date. When Sara confirms, she is assigned every Monday in the series, including dates she never accepted.
test_needed: Confirm an offer for the second of three recurring Mondays and assert no assignments exist for the other Mondays.

owner_question.question: When Sara accepts only the second Monday of Tom's recurring vacancy, what should be booked?
options: Only the accepted Monday
Require explicit acceptance of every date together
Every occurrence automatically (keep today's behaviour)

title: Upcoming bookings appear in completed-work history.
scenario: Tom books Sara for next week. Before Sara works the shift, both Tom's history and Sara's history already include it. Their completed-work lists therefore contain future commitments alongside past work.
test_needed: Create only a future assigned shift and assert both manager and worker history endpoints exclude it.

owner_question.question: Should Tom and Sara see next week's confirmed booking in History?
options: Only after the shift ends
In a separate clearly labelled upcoming section
Alongside completed work immediately (keep today's behaviour)

title: Shift lifecycle filters compare pharmacy clock times with UTC.
scenario: Sara finishes Tom's Sydney shift at 17:00. At 20:00 Sydney time, the filters compare its finish against the UTC morning clock and still classify it as upcoming. Tom and Sara continue seeing an ended booking as confirmed, and ended vacancies can remain active.
test_needed: Freeze time at 20:00 Sydney time for a same-day 17:00 finish and assert the shift is excluded from upcoming and active results.

owner_question.question: When Tom's pharmacy clock passes the shift's finish time, when should Sara's booking leave Upcoming?
options: At the finish time in that pharmacy's timezone
After a defined grace period in that pharmacy's timezone
When the UTC clock reaches the finish time (keep today's behaviour)

title: Named public shifts disclose internal pharmacy document links.
scenario: Tom uploads pharmacy procedures and controlled-drug protocols, then posts a named public vacancy. Sara opens the vacancy while merely browsing. Its response includes links to those internal documents before Tom has selected or booked her.
test_needed: Retrieve a named public shift as unrelated Sara and assert pharmacy procedure, protocol, and induction document links are absent.

owner_question.question: When should Sara gain access to Tom's internal pharmacy documents?
options: After a confirmed booking authorises access
Only after Tom explicitly grants access
Whenever she browses a named vacancy (keep today's behaviour)

title: Region admins cannot see other managers' shifts or cover requests at their assigned pharmacies.
scenario: Lina assigns Grace to manage Tom's pharmacy as a region admin with roster privileges, without adding a separate pharmacy-admin appointment. When Tom posts shifts, Grace's active, confirmed and history lists omit them, although the individual pharmacy permission check recognizes her authority. Omar's cover requests are also unavailable to Grace, preventing her from handling staffing work within her assigned region.
test_needed: Assign Grace roster-capable region membership without a PharmacyAdmin record; verify Tom's shifts and Omar's cover request are accessible only within her assigned pharmacies.

owner_question.question: When Lina gives Grace region-admin roster privileges for Tom's pharmacy, should Grace see Tom's shifts and decide Omar's cover requests?
options: Grace can manage this work through her region assignment.
Grace needs a separate pharmacy-admin appointment to manage others' work (keep today's behaviour).

title: Anonymous talent posts reveal the author's full name and user id to any signed-in account.
scenario: Sara posts her availability as anonymous, which is the default, because she is quietly looking for other work. Tom, or Zoe with a free account she just made, opens the logged-in talent feed or a single post. The server's answer carries Sara's full name and account id. Only the public feed hides them, so anonymity holds only for logged-out visitors.
test_needed: A signed-in owner fetches feed/ and retrieve for an is_anonymous post and must not receive explorer_name, author_user_id or explorer_user_id

owner_question.question: Sara posts anonymously. When Tom is logged in and looks at the talent board, what should he learn about who she is?
options: Nothing until Sara accepts his contact request
Name visible only to verified owners and organisation admins
Keep today: every logged-in user gets her full name and id

title: Work notes and calendar events can be moved into, or attached to, a pharmacy or organisation the person has no rights over.
scenario: Omar is an ordinary staff member at Tom's pharmacy. He edits one of his own work notes, changes its pharmacy to Nadia's pharmacy and assigns Nadia. The permission check only looks at the note's old pharmacy. The assignee check uses the new pharmacy, so it passes, and Nadia is notified with Omar's text. Separately, Tom can create an event naming his own pharmacy plus Lina's organisation. Only the pharmacy is checked, so the event appears in Lina's organisation calendar.
test_needed: A staff member PATCHes a work note with another pharmacy's id (expect 403 or no change); an owner POSTs an event with own pharmacy plus a foreign organisation (expect 403)

owner_question.question: Omar wants to move a work note from Tom's pharmacy to Nadia's pharmacy, and Tom tags an event with Lina's organisation. What should happen?
options: Never allowed: a note or event stays in the pharmacy or organisation it was made in
Allowed only if the person can manage both pharmacies or organisations
Keep today's behaviour

title: Deleting an account leaves the person's talent post live on the public and logged-in boards.
scenario: Sara deletes her ChemistTasker account. Her name, email and ID documents are removed, but her talent post is never touched: headline, free-text body, suburb, postcode and reference code stay. Logged-out visitors and owners like Tom keep seeing it, and a full-time post never expires. Tom may try to book or contact someone who has left the platform, and Sara's own words stay public after she asked to be removed.
test_needed: Delete an account that has an ExplorerPost, then public-feed/ and feed/ must not return that post

owner_question.question: Sara deletes her account while her availability post is on the talent board. What should happen to the post?
options: Delete the post along with the account
Hide it from every board but keep it for audit
Keep today: it stays visible

title: Fortnightly (and longer) weekly-repeat calendar items land on the wrong weeks in some months.
scenario: Tom sets a fortnightly 'controlled drug register check' work note starting Monday 2 March. When Omar opens a month whose first week is an odd number of weeks after 2 March, the note shows in the off weeks. Omar does the check in the wrong week and his ticks are saved against dates that are not real occurrences. Which weeks appear changes with the month being viewed.
test_needed: Weekly interval=2 from 2026-03-02, expanded for 2026-06-01..2026-06-30, must return 8 and 22 June, not 1, 15 and 29 June

owner_question.question: Tom sets a task to repeat every two weeks from 2 March. Which weeks should Omar see it in?
options: Always every second week counted from 2 March
Keep today: the weeks shift depending on the month viewed

title: A staff member born on 29 February stops birthday events for the rest of their pharmacy in non-leap years.
scenario: Ali was born on 29 February. In a non-leap year, the daily birthday job crashes when it reaches Ali, and the error is caught for the whole pharmacy. Every colleague processed after Ali, like Mia, gets no birthday entry on Tom's calendar all year.
test_needed: generate_birthday_events_for_pharmacy with a 29 February DOB and a 2027 target date must not raise, and must still create other staff members' events

owner_question.question: Ali's birthday is 29 February. In a non-leap year, what should Tom's calendar show?
options: Ali on 28 February, and everyone else as normal
Ali on 1 March, and everyone else as normal
Skip Ali that year, everyone else as normal

title: Password-reset links are copied into the user's in-app notifications, so anyone holding a signed-in session can take over the account without email access.
scenario: Mia stays signed in on the shared dispensary computer. A coworker goes to the public 'forgot password' page and enters Mia's email. The reset email also creates a 'Reset your password' notification in Mia's bell, and that notification holds the live reset link. The coworker opens it from Mia's session, sets a new password and locks Mia out, without ever touching her mailbox.
test_needed: POST password-reset/ for a known user, then assert that no Notification for that user has an action_url (or payload) containing the uid/token reset path.

owner_question.question: When someone asks for a password reset for Mia, what should Mia see inside the app?
options: Nothing in-app: the reset link goes by email only
An in-app alert 'A password reset was requested' with no link
Keep today's behaviour (notification carries the working reset link)

title: Asking for a mobile code again clears the verified-mobile flag, which unlocks the 'locked' mobile number and legal name while the profile keeps its Verified badge.
scenario: Sara has verified her mobile, and her profile is Verified with her AHPRA-matched name. She calls 'resend mobile code', which marks her mobile as unverified straight away. Now the lock checks no longer apply, so she requests a code for a new number under a different first and last name, and her name changes. Verified profiles are never automatically demoted, so Tom sees a Verified locum whose name and phone are not the ones that were checked.
test_needed: For a user with is_mobile_verified=True, POST mobile/resend-otp/ and then mobile/request-otp/ with a new number and new names; assert 400 and that the names and number are unchanged.

owner_question.question: Sara is already verified and asks for a new mobile code. What should happen to her verified mobile and name?
options: Resend is refused for an already-verified mobile; changes go through support
She can change the number, her Verified badge is removed until she re-verifies, and her name stays locked
Keep today's behaviour (resend unlocks the number and name, badge stays)

title: The invite endpoint can change an existing Org Admin's role, which skips the rule that every organisation keeps at least one Org Admin.
scenario: Lina is the only Org Admin of her chain. She, or the invite form, sends an organisation invite to her own email with the role Chief Admin. The invite finds her existing membership and overwrites its role without the 'must retain one Org Admin' check that normal edits run. The chain now has no Org Admin, and no Chief or Region Admin is allowed to create one.
test_needed: As the only ORG_ADMIN, POST the org invite with your own email and role CHIEF_ADMIN; assert 403 and that the membership role is still ORG_ADMIN.

owner_question.question: Lina sends an invite to someone who is already an admin of her organisation, possibly herself. What should the invite do?
options: Refuse it: existing members are changed only through the member edit screen
Allow the role change, but never if it leaves the organisation without an Org Admin
Keep today's behaviour (the invite silently overwrites the role)

title: Migration replaces historical invoice billing details with a customer matched only by name.
scenario: Sara has historical invoices for Tom's two pharmacies with the same bill-to name but different billing emails and addresses. During the upgrade, both invoices reuse one saved customer, and one invoice receives the other pharmacy's billing details. Resending that invoice can send it to the wrong pharmacy contact, including Nadia.
test_needed: Migrate two legacy invoices sharing a bill-to name but having different emails, addresses and ABNs; assert each migrated snapshot retains its original details.

owner_question.question: When Sara's historical invoices for Tom's pharmacies share a billing name, what should happen to their separate billing details during upgrade?
options: Preserve each invoice's original billing details
Require Sara to resolve conflicting customer details
Reuse one customer's details for both invoices (keep today's behaviour)

title: Editing an invoice leaves its separate super request at the old amount.
scenario: Sara creates an $800 service invoice and its separate $96 super request for Tom. She then corrects the service invoice to $400, making the super amount $48. The linked request remains $96, cannot be edited, and prevents creation of a corrected request, leaving Tom with an excessive contribution request.
test_needed: Create a separate super request, revise the parent's eligible amount downward, and assert the old contribution cannot remain the active request unchanged.

owner_question.question: When Sara corrects an invoice after creating Tom's super request, what should happen to that request?
options: Replace it through an audited correction
Block the invoice correction until the request is resolved
Keep the original super request unchanged (keep today's behaviour)

title: Invoice corrections leave previously recorded payment GST allocations unchanged.
scenario: Tom pays Sara $55 toward a $110 invoice containing $10 GST, so the payment records $5 GST. Sara corrects the invoice to GST-free while keeping the $110 total, then records Tom's remaining $55 payment. Her cash GST worksheet still includes the original $5 even though the corrected invoice contains no GST.
test_needed: Part-pay a GST invoice, revise it to GST-free at the same total, resend and settle it; assert cash GST is reconciled or the correction is rejected.

owner_question.question: When Sara corrects GST after Tom has partly paid, how should the recorded GST be handled?
options: Reconcile allocations through an audited adjustment
Require a separate correction before changing GST
Retain the original payment GST allocation (keep today's behaviour)

title: Marking an invoice paid leaves its payment balance and cash reporting unchanged.
scenario: Tom pays Sara's full invoice, and Sara selects Mark as paid as instructed by the screen. The invoice shows Paid, but its recorded payment amount stays zero and its outstanding balance remains the full amount. Sara's cash-basis GST worksheet also omits the money unless she separately records a payment.
test_needed: Mark an unpaid invoice paid through the normal action; assert zero balance and inclusion of the payment in the correct cash-reporting period.

owner_question.question: When Sara marks Tom's fully paid invoice as paid, what should happen to its balance and cash report?
options: Record the remaining payment with a payment date and clear Sara's balance
Require Sara to enter payment details before marking it paid
Change only the status and require a separate payment entry, as today

title: Finishing an older invoice email exposes a newer unsent revision.
scenario: Sara starts emailing an invoice to Tom, then saves a revised amount in another tab while the email is being sent. When the earlier email finishes, the app marks the latest invoice as sent even though that email contained the earlier revision. Tom can then see and approve Sara's newer draft before she sends it.
test_needed: Pause sending revision 1, save revision 2, then finish sending; assert revision 2 remains draft and Tom can see only revision 1.

owner_question.question: If Sara saves a newer draft while an earlier invoice email is sending to Tom, which revision should Tom see?
options: Only the emailed revision until Sara sends the newer draft
Prevent Sara from saving while the email is sending
Expose the newer draft when the earlier email finishes, as today

title: Extending an active employment agreement bypasses its junior rate expiry.
scenario: Tom creates junior employment terms for Mia ending before her next birthday, as the app requires. Once those terms have started, Tom can extend or clear their end date without the birthday check running again. Mia's later timesheets then carry the old junior rates beyond the required review date.
test_needed: Patch an already-started junior agreement to end on or after its birthday review date, including a null end date; assert rejection.

owner_question.question: When Tom extends Mia's junior employment terms across her next birthday, what should happen?
options: Require successor terms with reviewed rates from Mia's birthday
Automatically create successor terms using the new age
Continue Mia's frozen junior rates beyond her birthday, as today

title: The invoice issue action fails on PostgreSQL because it locks outside a transaction.
scenario: Sara confirms a saved invoice using the supported issue action before sending it. The confirmation attempts a database lock without opening a transaction, so PostgreSQL rejects the request and Sara receives a server error. The isolated SQLite tests do not expose this failure.
test_needed: Call the issue action on PostgreSQL from a TransactionTestCase without an enclosing transaction; assert successful confirmation rather than TransactionManagementError.

owner_question.question: When Sara confirms a saved invoice through the existing issue action, what should happen?
options: Confirm successfully while allowing later edits
Retire the action and direct Sara to the current send flow
Keep the existing action and its current failure

title: Replacement approval keeps the departing worker's payment terms
scenario: Omar requests a swap with Ben, Tom's favourite locum with an accepted pharmacy membership. Tom unpublishes the shift and approves the swap. Ben inherits Omar's employment and payment terms, and his rate is recalculated from Omar's agreement without recording Ben's own accepted terms.
test_needed: Attempt to replace Omar's payroll assignment with Ben's locum membership; verify approval cannot transfer Omar's employment snapshot to Ben.

owner_question.question: When Tom approves Ben replacing Omar, how should Ben's payment terms be established?
options: Require Ben to accept his own offer and payment terms
Restrict direct replacements to employed staff and use their own dated agreements
Give Ben Omar's existing terms (keep today's behaviour)

title: Coverage checks mark partly staffed intervals as fully covered
scenario: Tom requires one pharmacist from 09:00 to 17:00 and schedules Omar only from 09:00 to 10:00. The coverage panel reports the whole requirement as covered with no shortfall. Tom can therefore overlook seven hours with no pharmacist scheduled.
test_needed: Configure one pharmacist required from 09:00 to 17:00 with Omar assigned only 09:00 to 10:00; verify coverage reports a shortfall.

owner_question.question: Should Tom's 09:00–17:00 pharmacist requirement count as covered when Omar works only 09:00–10:00?
options: Show uncovered hours and a coverage shortfall
Show partial coverage requiring Tom's review
Mark the whole interval covered (keep today's behaviour)

title: Old acknowledgements prevent workers acknowledging a republished roster
scenario: Omar acknowledges Tom's published roster. Tom unpublishes the week, changes it and publishes it again. Tom sees Omar as awaiting acknowledgement, but Omar still sees the roster as acknowledged and has no acknowledgement button.
test_needed: After Omar acknowledges a week, unpublish and republish it; verify his worker response reports acknowledgement pending and the acknowledgement action remains available.

owner_question.question: After Tom changes and republishes an acknowledged week, what should Omar see?
options: A pending acknowledgement for the new publication
A pending acknowledgement only if Omar's shifts changed
His previous acknowledgement remains sufficient (keep today's worker behaviour)

title: Coworker roster responses expose private leave notes
scenario: Omar submits a pending sick-leave request linked to a published shift and explains his medical circumstances in the note. Mia opens the pharmacy roster as an ordinary accepted staff member. The response includes Omar's leave type and full private note, although the leave endpoint restricts Mia to her own requests.
test_needed: As Mia, retrieve Omar's roster assignment containing a pending sick-leave note; verify the response excludes his private leave details.

owner_question.question: What should Mia see about Omar's leave when viewing their shared pharmacy roster?
options: Only a generic availability or cover indicator
The leave status and type, with the note restricted to Omar and managers
The full leave note (keep today's behaviour)

title: Locked manifests omit every payroll assignment
scenario: Tom enables payroll and approves Omar's timesheet for shifts designated for payroll. Locking the period succeeds, but the returned manifest contains no payroll assignments or payroll work days. Invoice and timesheet-only routing lists are also empty because the saved timesheet lacks the roster details that locking reads.
test_needed: Build and approve a payroll-enabled period containing Omar's PAYROLL assignment, then lock it and assert that its assignment and worked day are present in payroll_export.

owner_question.question: When Tom locks a payroll-enabled period containing Omar's approved payroll shifts, what should the locked record contain?
options: Omar's payroll assignments and approved work days
Reject locking until payroll routing is available
An empty payroll export despite those assignments (keep today's behaviour)

title: Changing contracted hours leaves rebuilt timesheets showing the previous hours
scenario: Tom changes Omar's contracted week from 38 hours to 30 hours after a timesheet has been built. The change schedules a rebuild, but ordinary rebuilding treats the inputs as unchanged and keeps the old 38-hour total. The timesheet is then marked current and can retain its previous approval.
test_needed: Build Omar's weekly timesheet with 2280 contracted minutes, change only the setting to 1800, rebuild without force, and assert the current total and revision reflect 1800.

owner_question.question: When Tom changes Omar's contracted hours for an open timesheet period, what should recalculation do?
options: Update the hours and require review of the changed revision
Keep existing periods unchanged through an explicit effective-date policy
Mark the timesheet current while retaining its old hours (keep today's behaviour)

title: Timesheets treat individually withdrawn roster shifts as published work
scenario: Tom withdraws Omar's shift from a published week and edits its hours before republishing it. Omar's roster correctly hides the shift, but recalculating his timesheet still includes the withdrawn shift and its draft hours. It can also raise a missing-attendance blocker for work Omar was no longer shown as scheduled.
test_needed: Withdraw Omar's individual shift while its week stays published, edit it, rebuild his timesheet, and assert the withdrawn assignment contributes no roster minutes or missing-attendance blocker.

owner_question.question: While Tom edits a withdrawn shift that Omar cannot see in his roster, what should Omar's timesheet use?
options: Exclude the withdrawn shift until Tom republishes it
Preserve the last published hours until Tom republishes it
Use the unpublished draft hours immediately (keep today's behaviour)

title: Overnight attendance corrections leave the next period approved with stale minutes
scenario: Omar works from Sunday night into Monday morning, with the two parts recorded in consecutive timesheet periods. After both are approved, Tom corrects Monday's finish time from 06:00 to 07:00. Only the period containing Sunday's clock-in is marked for rebuilding; Monday's period keeps its old approved minutes and can be locked without the extra hour.
test_needed: Approve both periods intersecting Omar's Sunday-to-Monday session, correct Monday's clock-out, and assert Monday's timesheet becomes stale and cannot lock before rebuilding and reapproval.

owner_question.question: When Tom corrects Omar's overnight attendance spanning two open timesheet periods, which periods should require recalculation?
options: Every period whose worked minutes or checks are affected
Reject the correction until Tom explicitly reopens all affected periods
Only the period containing the original clock-in (keep today's behaviour)

title: Archiving a roster removes its scheduled work and approved leave from timesheets
scenario: Tom approves Omar's annual leave against a published roster, then archives that completed roster week before locking the timesheet period. Archiving triggers recalculation, but archived weeks are excluded from the timesheet's roster inputs. Omar's approved leave minutes fall to zero even though the leave remains approved and the archived roster remains visible as published history.
test_needed: Build a timesheet with approved roster-linked annual leave, archive its published roster week, rebuild, and assert rostered and approved-leave minutes remain unchanged.

owner_question.question: When Tom archives a completed published roster, what should happen to Omar's scheduled hours and approved leave in its open timesheet period?
options: Preserve them as historical published work
Require Tom to lock the timesheet period before archiving
Remove the roster hours and reduce scheduled leave to zero (keep today's behaviour)

title: Extending an active junior agreement bypasses its birthday rate limit.
scenario: Tom creates Mia's junior pay agreement ending before her next birthday. After it starts, he removes the end date, and the save succeeds while preserving her lower rates. Work after her birthday can now use those rates without requiring updated terms.
test_needed: For an active junior agreement ending before the next birthday, PATCH effective_to=null and assert rejection with the original end date preserved.

owner_question.question: When Tom extends Mia's junior agreement beyond her next birthday, what should happen?
options: Require new dated terms for Mia from her birthday
Automatically apply Mia's updated birthday rates
Preserve Mia's existing lower rates indefinitely (keep today's behaviour)

title: Saving employment terms leaves existing timesheets using stale pay agreements.
scenario: Tom approves Omar's timesheet, then records a higher rate effective today while the pay period remains open. Omar's existing timesheet keeps the previous pay agreement and remains approved. Tom can lock the period without recalculating or reviewing the changed terms.
test_needed: After approving Omar's timesheet containing today's work, create successor terms effective today and assert locking fails until recalculation and renewed approval.

owner_question.question: When Tom changes Omar's pay terms for dates in an approved but unlocked timesheet, what should happen?
options: Require recalculation and renewed approval for Omar's affected timesheet
Prevent the change until Tom explicitly reopens Omar's timesheet
Allow locking Omar's existing terms until someone manually recalculates (keep today's behaviour)

title: Referee decline links cannot complete the browser flow.
scenario: Omar asks Tom to provide a reference. Tom clicks the decline link in the email, but its signed-token address does not match the browser page. The browser operation also calls an obsolete address, so Tom cannot record his refusal.
test_needed: Follow Omar's actual emailed decline link as Tom and verify it records rejection through the signed-token endpoint.

owner_question.question: When Tom clicks the decline link for Omar's reference request, what should happen?
options: Record Tom's refusal and show confirmation
Ask Tom to confirm before recording refusal
Leave Tom unable to decline through the link (keep today's behaviour)

title: Renaming a group on mobile silently removes its other members.
scenario: Tom renames a custom group containing Omar and Mia using the mobile app. Saving the name also removes Omar and Mia from the group because the omitted member selection becomes an empty replacement list. Tom remains as creator, while Omar and Mia lose access.
test_needed: Rename Tom's group without supplying participants and verify Omar and Mia remain participants.

owner_question.question: When Tom changes only a group's name, what should happen to Omar and Mia?
options: Keep Omar and Mia in the group
Require Tom to confirm any membership changes
Remove everyone except Tom (keep today's behaviour)

title: Mobile group member search cannot find returned participants.
scenario: Tom opens mobile group creation and searches for Omar, who is available in his chat contacts. Omar's name is returned inside his identity details, but the search checks a different location and shows no match. Tom cannot select Omar to create the group or add him to an existing group.
test_needed: Return Omar with a nested user identity, search his name in mobile group creation, and verify he is selectable.

owner_question.question: When Tom searches for Omar among available mobile group contacts, what should happen?
options: Find Omar by his displayed name
Show all available contacts for Tom to select
Return no matches for nested contact names (keep today's behaviour)

title: Collection helpers silently discard records after the first page
scenario: Tom schedules 60 assignments at his pharmacy for one week. The roster screens receive only the first 50, so Omar's assignment can disappear from his schedule even though it remains booked. The same pagination loss hides later membership records, pharmacies, shift history and Hub comments.
test_needed: Return 50 roster assignments with a next page containing Omar's assignment; assert the complete roster includes his assignment.

owner_question.question: When Tom's weekly roster exceeds 50 assignments, how should Omar access all his scheduled work?
options: Load the complete weekly roster automatically
Provide explicit pagination with the full assignment count
Show only the first 50 assignments (keep today's behaviour)

title: Booked pharmacist cards can show a different rate from the agreed pay
scenario: Tom posts a shift with a $65 weekday rate and an $80 Saturday rate. Sara accepts the Saturday work at $80 per hour. Her confirmed and history cards on web and mobile can still say $65 per hour fixed because they use the shift's general rate rather than her agreed pay.
test_needed: Give Sara an accepted Saturday assignment at $80 with the shift's fixed rate at $65; assert her booked pay label does not show $65.

owner_question.question: What should Sara's booked-shift card show when her accepted Saturday rate differs from Tom's general advertised rate?
options: Sara's agreed rate for each booked date
A prompt to view agreed pay without an advertised-rate label
Tom's general advertised rate (keep today's behaviour)

title: Editing a shift description breaks its pending offers.
scenario: Tom offers Sara one date, then edits only the shift description before Sara accepts. Saving replaces the existing dates and detaches Sara's offer from its date. Sara's offer remains pending, but attempting to accept it fails.
test_needed: Create a pending offer for Sara with single_user_only=false, submit the description-edit payload, and assert its original slot remains linked and accept succeeds.

owner_question.question: When Tom edits only a shift description after offering a date to Sara, what should happen to Sara's offer?
options: Preserve Sara's offer and its original date
Block Tom's edit until outstanding offers are withdrawn
Leave Sara's offer pending but unusable (keep today's behaviour)

title: Automatic escalation can expose shifts earlier than the selected interval.
scenario: Tom in Perth selects automatic escalation from his pharmacy's locum audience to the public board after 24 hours in October. The submitted time has no timezone, so the server interprets it as Sydney time. Sara can see the vacancy three hours earlier than Tom selected.
test_needed: With the client in Australia/Perth and Django in Australia/Sydney during October, assert a 24-hour automatic escalation persists exactly 24 hours after the starting instant.

owner_question.question: When Tom in Perth chooses public visibility after 24 hours, when should Sara gain access?
options: After the full 24 hours Tom selected
At a pharmacy-local time explicitly shown to Tom
At the submitted Sydney time regardless of Tom's timezone (keep today's behaviour)

title: The finance warning not to resend an invoice email is replaced by a generic error, and the test that should catch this never runs.
scenario: Sara emails an invoice to Tom's pharmacy and the mail provider times out. The server marks the email as uncertain and replies 'Email acceptance is uncertain. Do not resend until checked with your mail provider.' Sara sees only 'Request failed with status 503', so she doesn't know her email may already have gone out, and she may keep pressing Send or think nothing was sent. The test file that checks this message is kept is not run by any script and depends on a setup function that now does nothing, so the problem goes unnoticed.
test_needed: A finance send call that gets a 503 with the uncertain-delivery detail must reject with that detail text, not the generic status message.

owner_question.question: When Sara sends Tom an invoice email and the server can't confirm it was delivered, what should Sara see?
options: The server's exact warning: delivery is uncertain, do not resend
A fixed in-app message, 'Delivery uncertain, check before resending', shown for this 503 only
Keep the generic 'Request failed with status 503' and rely on the server blocking a second send

title: Worker leave request submission always fails due to reading nonexistent membership id from session user
scenario: Omar logs into the web dashboard and opens My Leave to submit annual leave for his shifts at Tom's pharmacy. The pharmacy selector assigns an undefined membership value because pharmacy memberships in the session profile omit the membership record identifier. When Omar submits the form, the server receives a missing membership parameter and rejects the request with a permission error, completely blocking him from requesting leave.
test_needed: Submit a leave request from MyLeavePage using an authenticated worker whose profile memberships contain pharmacy details without an id attribute, asserting that a valid membership identifier is supplied to the API rather than null or NaN.

owner_question.question: When Omar requests leave on the web dashboard, how should the application identify his active pharmacy membership?
options: Include the membership primary key on pharmacy memberships in the user profile payload so Omar's leave request submits a valid membership identifier.
Update the leave creation endpoint to accept the pharmacy identifier directly and resolve Omar's active membership automatically.
Require workers to submit leave requests through mobile or ask Tom to enter it directly (keep today's behaviour).

title: Timesheet detail drawer renders manager check resolution and punch actions in worker mode
scenario: Omar opens My Hours to review his worked hours at Tom's pharmacy and inspects a timesheet with an attendance warning. Because the details drawer fails to pass worker mode into check cards, Omar is shown active Resolve and Waive buttons as well as an Add missing clock time button. When Omar attempts to resolve the check or add a missing clock time, the request is rejected with a 403 error because only pharmacy managers like Tom may approve or waive attendance checks.
test_needed: Render TimesheetDetailDrawer with managerMode set to false and verify that CheckCard renders in read-only mode without Resolve, Waive, Reopen, or Add missing clock time buttons.

owner_question.question: When Omar reviews his own hours in the timesheet details drawer, how should checks and attendance issues be displayed?
options: Display checks in read-only mode with instructions for Omar to contact his manager Tom to correct source attendance.
Allow Omar to submit explanations as comments on the timesheet without showing direct resolution or waiving controls.
Leave the manager resolution and punch buttons visible to workers even though server permissions reject their submissions (keep today's behaviour).

title: Post-verification and dashboard return links navigate to an unrouted root path, landing users on a 404 page
scenario: After Zoe (or Sara, Ali, or Mia) finishes verifying her mobile number on the web onboarding flow, the page promises to redirect her to her dashboard. Instead, it assigns the browser location to /dashboard, where React Router finds no matching route and displays the 404 Page Not Found screen. The same 404 occurs when Sara clicks 'My dashboard' after submitting a membership application or when clicking subscription buttons as a non-owner.
test_needed: Mount the router at '/dashboard' with an authenticated user and assert that it redirects to the user's role-specific dashboard instead of rendering NotFoundPage.

owner_question.question: When an authenticated user lands on or is redirected to '/dashboard', where should the app send them?
options: (Recommended) Redirect '/dashboard' to the user's role-specific dashboard overview via resolveDashboardPath.
Update each caller individually to construct the role dashboard path before navigating.
Keep today's behaviour where '/dashboard' falls through to the 404 Page Not Found screen.

title: Attendance timeline correction modal uses UTC string in local datetime input shifting timestamps
scenario: Omar clocks out at 5:00 PM at Tom's pharmacy in Sydney. When Tom clicks to correct Omar's clock-out time on the review page, the date-time picker is populated with a universal time string showing 7:00 AM instead of 5:00 PM. When Tom submits the form, the browser parses the value in the local timezone, shifting the record 10 hours earlier so it precedes Omar's morning clock-in. The server rejects the submission for violating event order, blocking Tom from saving corrections, or silently distorts shift hours if editing clock-in.
test_needed: In a browser running in Australia/Sydney (UTC+10), opening the correction modal for an event at 17:00 local time and submitting should send an effective timestamp of 17:00 AEST (07:00Z) rather than shifting 10 hours to 07:00 AEST (21:00Z previous day).

owner_question.question: When Tom corrects an attendance clock time on the review page, how should the date-time picker initialize and submit timestamps for Australian pharmacies?
options: (Recommended) Pre-fill the picker in the pharmacy's local timezone and submit the local time converted to UTC, preserving the intended hours.
Pre-fill the picker with UTC time and require managers to manually calculate timezone offsets.
Keep today's behaviour where UTC strings are loaded into local datetime pickers and shifted on submission.

title: Shared shift landing redirect produces non-existent dashboard routes for non-standard roles
scenario: Tom creates a shared shift link for an open shift at his pharmacy. When Lina, an organisation admin, clicks the link while logged in, the page calculates a non-existent role path. The application fails to match any valid screen and displays a missing page error, preventing Lina from reviewing the shift. The same breakdown locks out users with pharmacy manager roles.
test_needed: Assert that an authenticated user with role ORG_STAFF or PHARMACY_MANAGER navigating to /shifts/link?token=... is not redirected to a non-existent route resulting in a 404 error.

owner_question.question: When Lina (organisation admin) or a pharmacy manager opens a shared shift link while logged in, where should the platform take them?
options: (Recommended) Redirect them to their organisation's shift center (/dashboard/organization/shifts/:id) or keep them on the shared shift details view.
Do not redirect logged-in admins away from the public shift view, rendering the shared shift directly.
Keep today's behaviour where they are redirected to /dashboard/orgstaff/shifts/:id resulting in a 404.

title: Accepting one date hides the remaining dates of a counter offer
scenario: Sara proposes different rates for two dates in Tom's shift. Tom accepts the first date, and the whole proposal disappears because it is marked accepted and removed from the list. Tom can no longer review or accept Sara's proposed terms for the second date through the normal screen.

owner_question.question: When Tom accepts the first of two dates proposed by Sara, what should happen to her second date?
options: Keep Sara's second date available for a separate decision
Accept both dates together with an explicit confirmation
Hide Sara's remaining proposal after the first acceptance (keep today's behaviour)

title: Jobs without dated slots never load internal candidates
scenario: Tom posts a full-time job without individual dated slots, and Omar expresses interest in the whole job. Tom opens the internal candidates view, but it says nobody has responded. The page never requests the job's internal candidates because there are no dates to iterate over.

owner_question.question: When Omar applies to Tom's full-time job without dated slots, what should Tom see?
options: Show Omar in the job's internal candidates
Require dated slots before Tom can publish the job
Show an empty internal candidates list (keep today's behaviour)

title: Editing chain details removes its pharmacy links
scenario: Tom has both pharmacies in his chain and changes only the chain's contact email or logo. Saving replaces the chain's pharmacy selection with an empty list, so both pharmacies disappear from the chain. Nadia consequently loses the chain connection used to reach staff at Tom's other pharmacy.

owner_question.question: When Tom edits only his chain's email or logo, what should happen to its pharmacies?
options: Keep every existing pharmacy linked
Require Tom to confirm the pharmacy selection before saving
Remove all pharmacy links (keep today's behaviour)

title: Notification refreshes leave counter offers stale
scenario: Tom opens a shift before Sara submits a counter offer, leaving an empty offer list cached. Sara then submits her proposal, and Tom opens its notification while staying in the Active screen. The shift and interests reload, but the counter-offer list stays empty, so Sara's proposed terms remain unavailable until Tom reloads or leaves and reopens the screen.

owner_question.question: When Tom opens Sara's new counter-offer notification from an already open shift, what should happen?
options: Refresh and display Sara's proposed terms
Show a visible refresh action that loads Sara's proposal
Require Tom to reload or reopen the screen (keep today's behaviour)

title: Organisation and pharmacy admins are treated as invoice issuers instead of recipients on legacy invoice detail view
scenario: Sara completes a shift for Tom's pharmacy, which is managed by Lina at the organisation level and Grace as the pharmacy admin, and issues an invoice. options: Display the read-only recipient invoice with pay-to bank details, 'Mark as paid', and 'Report an issue' actions
Restrict invoice review and payment marking strictly to the pharmacy owner (Tom)
Outcome C (keep today's behaviour)

title: Pharmacy owner cannot view or respond to organization claim requests because the review section is hidden when no pharmacies are already claimed

Outcome B: Direct Tom from email and alerts to a dedicated claim requests page rather than embedding it inside the pharmacies list.

options: Keep Omar's original shift and create the separate shift

options: Remove the saved rate so new postings have no late-night default

title: Cancelling a convert-to-open-shift edit leaves the old shift marked for deletion, so a later, unrelated open-shift post deletes it.
